clue.text: Hold out to spike policeman's shoe

indicators.note: to spike something is to drive into it, so the scrambled letters pierce the other word

parts.note: copper is slang for a policeman

indicators.note: out signals the letters of hold are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone resisting the urge to puncture a constable's boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the first word, and 'to spike' drives the result into the slang word for a constable just after its opening letter; 'shoe' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a large heavy boot, the kind of footwear a plodding person wears.

clue.text: 23 admits initially entering into spirit of fun

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the word takes other letters inside it

parts.note: the answer to 23 across means tempt, and a synonym of that is lure

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Something tempting lets newcomers into the party spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives E, I and S, which 'admits' places inside LURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time spent on enjoyment, so it stands for fun or recreation.

clue.text: A dark, poor place in Africa

indicators.note: poor suggests something badly made, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A gloomy, impoverished African town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges the letters of A DARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Dakar is the capital city of Senegal on the West African coast.

clue.text: Isn't MacDuff in a hole? There's a source of material

definitions.text: Isn't MacDuff in a hole? There's a source of material

parts.words: Isn't MacDuff in a hole? There's a source of material
parts.note: plays on 'Lay on, Macduff': a quarry where the overburden is laid open to the sky, so the digger works in no closed hole, yet ore and stone come out of it

explanation.surface: A theatregoer wonders whether the Shakespearean thane is trapped in a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Macbeth character is a red herring; the clue describes surface extraction, where workings are open to the sky rather than in a tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: Surface extraction removes ore or coal from an open pit, a large source of raw material.

clue.text: Constabulary admits flipping coin: heads for evil in disguise

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the force word holds other letters inside it

parts.note: a constabulary is a police force

indicators.note: flipping suggests tossing over and over, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Police officers let a coin be tossed to settle things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like mild British slang for annoyance, but it scrambles the two words after it; 'admits' sets that jumble inside the force, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisoned chalice is an apparent gift or honour that turns out to be harmful, an evil thing dressed up as good.

clue.text: Defeat royal device for data delivery

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a royal cipher

explanation.surface: A monarch is beaten by a piece of computer kit.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the cipher of Queen Elizabeth, a standard crossword stand-in for royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A router is a networking box that forwards packets of information between computers.

clue.text: Wolves matured in a box

parts.note: wolves hunt together in a pack
matured means aged, as with cheese or wine

explanation.surface: Old wolves are kept confined in a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something packaged has been wrapped or sealed in a container for sale.

clue.text: As a contribution to a rising economy, no dues paid to Goliath, for one

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom upwards
a contribution to something is a part of it, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A setter pays no dues as their part in a growing economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a contribution to' finds MYNODUESP inside ECONOMY NO DUES PAID, and 'rising' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath is the setter's pen-name, the false name under which this crossword is published.

clue.text: Start off at 17, from having a change of heart to toe the line

indicators.note: start off means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: the answer to 17 across means famous person, and a synonym of that is icon

indicators.note: the heart of the word from is its middle, and those central letters change places

explanation.surface: A guide on how to obey orders, beginning at line seventeen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' takes the I from ICON to leave CON; 'having a change of heart' swaps the middle R and O of FROM to give FORM.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to follow the rules or behave as expected, to obey or comply.

clue.text: Monica heard Nikki?

definitions.meaning: said out loud, Monica sounds like moniker
Nikki is a pet form of a ... like Nicola, so the question mark marks an example

explanation.definitionFit: A moniker is an informal name, and Nikki is a familiar shortening of Nicola.

clue.text: Runs a piece about gourmets

indicators.note: about can mean around in a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone runs a news piece on fine diners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' scrambles RUNS A PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicureans are devoted to refined sensuous pleasure, especially good food and drink.

clue.text: Polish and almost wealthy, getting a distinguished title

parts.note: to polish is to rub

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A Pole who is nearly rich acquires a grand title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' clips RICH to RIC. 'Polish' is a verb here, not the nationality its capital suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a heading printed in red in old manuscripts, set apart from the rest of the text.

clue.text: Unrestricted love to die penniless outside

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O

indicators.note: outside means the word goes around the other

parts.note: penniless means poor
to die is to end

explanation.surface: A lover is fated to die broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the word for penniless around the word for die. Love is O from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-door policy is one of free access with no barriers or limits.

clue.text: Please remove my blindfold, hmmm?

definitions.meaning: a literal request to be allowed to look
a thinking noise, said while pondering a question

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a plea to be allowed sight and a filler used while considering something.

clue.text: Network-covered home towards the back not a feature of 4, 21

indicators.note: covered means the second word sits under the first, wrapped by it

parts.note: a network of threads is a mesh
in means at home
aft means at or towards the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A house wrapped in netting, viewed from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' wraps the network round the home word. The definition is fair because surface workings at 4 down and 21 down need no vertical tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical tunnel sunk to reach coal is used in deep pits, never in open quarry workings.

clue.text: See 9
Favourite able queen uncovered dye mixture

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters are stripped away, leaving the inside
mixture signals that the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A capable queen's hair dye is revealed as a blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' gives BL and UEE; 'mixture' turns DYE into YED.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-eyed boy is a person in favour, the one most liked by those in charge.

clue.text: Famous person tucking into chilli con carne

indicators.note: tucking into means eating into, so the letters are inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A celebrity is digging into a spicy bean stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' finds the answer in CHILLI CON.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a celebrated person admired as a symbol of something.

clue.text: Two PCs deployed to contain a Jersey product

indicators.note: to contain means to hold inside, so one piece goes into the other
deployed means sent out in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two police constables are sent out to keep a Channel Island export in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges TWO PCS, and 'to contain' puts A inside it. A Jersey is a breed of dairy cow from the Channel Island of Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: Dung is what a Jersey cow produces, a humorous kind of output.

clue.text: Jane Austen's life, a memoir starts appearing in London, perhaps

indicators.note: appearing in means the letters are placed inside another word

parts.note: London is an example of a city

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A biography of the novelist is published in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes initials, and 'appearing in' puts them inside the example of a city after its first letter. The definition goes with Calamity Jane, the American frontierswoman, not the novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamity Jane was the nickname of Martha Jane Canary, the Wild West scout.

clue.text: See 24
See 4
An outfit cuts retrogressive political symbol

indicators.note: retrogressive means going backwards, so the whole run is read in reverse

parts.note: an gives the article A
an outfit or set of gear is a kit
saws means cuts

explanation.surface: A uniform shears through a backward-looking party's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrogressive' reverses AKITSAWS to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked cross was the emblem of the German Nazi party.

clue.text: Tempt conservative to shift right in full

indicators.note: to shift right in means the conservative letter displaces the one for right inside the word

parts.note: full means entire, complete

explanation.surface: Persuade a Tory to move fully rightwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shift' replaces the R in ENTIRE with C.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or attract someone by offering pleasure.

clue.text: They're needed to get on board with Kent artistic production

definitions.text: They're needed to get on board

indicators.note: a production is something made, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: An arts staging in Kent that you need passes for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges KENT ARTISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway passes are what passengers must hold to ride on a carriage.

clue.text: Brown primarily chosen as PM after Blair's invasion levelled Iraq twice? Yes!

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown is picked as Prime Minister after Blair's invasion flattened Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the first letter of each word from CHOSEN to YES. The definition is Capability Brown, the English landscape gardener, disguised as the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot Brown, the eighteenth-century landscape gardener, was nicknamed for his talk of a site's potential.

clue.text: See 7 across
Hey, frames for pictures? Sweet!

indicators.note: frames are what surround something, so the first and last letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Someone admires photo frames and calls them lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frames for' takes the first and last letters of PICTURES and SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A whispered call to attract someone's attention, like an informal hello.

clue.text: Why poor Serge is stuffed with eats

definitions.text: Why poor Serge is stuffed with eats

indicators.note: stuffed with means filled, so the jumbled word holds the other inside
poor suggests something in bad shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: dines means eats

explanation.surface: An explanation of why a man named Serge overate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' jumbles the name, and 'is stuffed with' fills it with the word for eats, before its last letter. The whole clue also explains the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is the reason a person ends up overfull of food.
